notes.text: Dylan DeMelo is on injured reserve, reported after he played in their last game.
Elias Salomonsson is away for personal reasons and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Bowen Byram is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 29% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 119:11 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Patrick Kane returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Dillon Boucher was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Cole Smith and Ryan Greene.

story.head: The Jets are on a heater
paras: The Blackhawks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in overtime in Chicago on Oct 15. The Blackhawks (5-13-1) beat Buffalo 3-2 in overtime on Thursday. The Jets have won five straight, the last an 8-3 rout of Dallas, and they’re rolling. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Jets sixth (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Hawks last (31st).

The Jets’ record (.525) is about what their chances are worth. The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.289) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .374, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Jets ice the puck less than anyone (1st), create chances on the penalty kill (3rd) and get their shots through to the net (3rd). On the other side, the Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest) and don't block many shots (31st). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so the Jets have the edge over them on the power play. Chicago has scored 2.21 goals a game, the fewest in the league, and allowed 4.11, the second most.

Kyle Connor (16 G / 8 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the Jets in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (6 G / 16 A / 22 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind, with ten points in his last five games. For the Blackhawks, Connor Bedard (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 19 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Stuart Skinner (7-4-3 / .886 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Winnipeg, and Spencer Knight (5-10-0 / .883 SV% in 15 GS) for Chicago.
